content:
President Donald Trump was given a fairly typical holiday question during a Thanksgiving telephone Q&A session with U.S. service members.

But he delivered anything but a typical answer.

“What are you most thankful for as the president and personally?” the U.S. Marine sergeant on the line asked.

Trump called it a “beautiful question,” but didn’t quite offer a direct response, nor did he mention his family, his health or even the U.S. service members calling into the event.

(Story continues below video.)

“I oftentimes will be asked that question and I campaigned on a concept and a theme that was very successful, ‘Make America Great Again,’ and that’s what I want,” he said, adding:

“I want to make America great again, greater than ever before, and we’re very close to being there. We are, as of the election, we created a value in terms of stock markets, we have the highest stock markets in history. We broke the record from day one in less than two years, 88 times. And it’s been amazing, so we’re gonna see amazing things over the next period of time.”

He also predicted a “very bipartisan relationship” with the incoming Democratic majority in Congress and said he hopes to “take care of a lot of different things,” including health care.

“I have the power of veto and I’m not looking to use it but it’s a very strong power,” he added, hours after he posted a meme of himself as “Veto Corleone” using a giant veto stamp. “I’m not looking to veto everything for two years and that’s not what they want either. So I have a feeling we’re gonna have a great relationship and a lot of things are going to get done maybe more than would have gotten done the more traditional way.”

Trump never did directly name what he was thankful for.
